title: Eng leads ops workshop — risk burn & canary plan
content:
Date: 2028-11-02
Facilitator: Evelyn Park
Duration: 60m (compact ops workshop format)

Attendees:
- Evelyn Park (owner)
- Marcus Li (serving-runtime)
- Rina Kapoor (platform infra)
- Omar Haddad (SRE)
- Sofia Torres (product-hosted-api PM)
- Jae Kim (solutions eng)
- Joined mid-session: Priya Shah (security)

Goals for this meeting:
- Rapid risk triage for the next 6-week launch window (Dedicated capacity v2)
- Finalize canary rollback/step policies for multi-region rollout
- Identify 1–2 quick mitigations to reduce SRE on-call noise this sprint

Top-line summary / decisions:
- We accepted a trimmed canary plan: 3-stage rollout (internal -> beta customers -> full regional ramp) with explicit circuit-breaker thresholds (latency P95 > 350ms OR error rate > 0.6% for 5m triggers rollback). Decision owner: Marcus.
- Prioritized risk burn list and agreed on a focused 6-week backlog: (1) KV cache invalidation edge-case, (2) autoscaler cold-start flakiness, (3) fallback-model mismatch diagnostics. Rina and Omar to co-own remediation tracks.
- Immediate SRE noise reduction: implement a temporary suppressor for noisy alerts from batch-encoder nodes until infra fix lands (suppress window: 12h/day) — temporary mitigations only, not permanent. Owner: Omar.

Notes / discussion highlights:
- Canary thresholds rationale: product needs a conservative latency bound because many customers are using hosted real-time chat — P95 target set at 350ms for this canary (product + SRE compromise). Sofia emphasized importance of token-level cost tracking during canary to spot cost regressions.
- KV cache invalidation: observed in JIRA-ENG-7891 — rare path where prefix mismatch causes stale responses for ~0.03% of requests under specific batching. Correlated to a recent kernel-selection tweak. Rina: patch candidate available, test harness failing intermittently. Next step: reproduce with 1M synthetic prefix combos.
- Autoscaler cold-starts: intermittent backlog in Dedicated pools when burst policy triggers. Root cause likely resource exhaustion on instance-image pull and containerd timeouts. Quick win: increase parallel image pull limit and prioritize warm pool size by +15% for the first 48h of canary ramp.
- Fallback-model mismatch: customer reports during fallback (small->quantized variant) that hallucination rate spikes on a specific prompt family. Action: run targeted evals against the fallback variant with customers' prompt set (Sofia + Solutions).

Escalations / blockers:
- Compliance readiness (Private deployments): Priya flagged outstanding audit artefacts for the new on-prem packaging. These are blockers for a pilot customer (Legal deadline 2028-11-20). Owner: Priya to coordinate with Product and Solutions; concrete list in Confluence-1423.
- Dedicated infra capacity forecasting: Finance needs a committed-headcount/instance forecast for Q1 2029 by 2028-11-09 for renewal quotes. Rina + Marcus to prepare a short two-slide forecast.

Action items (owner — due):
1) Marcus Li — finalize canary circuit-breaker config and add automated rollback runbook to runbooks repo (GH PR: infra/pull/598). Due: 2028-11-05.
2) Rina Kapoor + Omar Haddad — reproduce KV cache invalidation at scale and validate patch candidate; add test matrix. Due: 2028-11-09.
3) Omar Haddad — deploy temporary alert suppressor for batch-encoder node noise and produce incident log sampler for review. Due: 2028-11-04.
4) Sofia Torres + Jae Kim — run customer prompt evals against fallback-model; compile a short regression report and mitigation recommendations. Due: 2028-11-07.
5) Priya Shah — publish compliance artifact checklist for Private pilot and schedule weekly checkpoint with Legal. Due: 2028-11-06.
6) Marcus + Rina — two-slide capacity & cost forecast for Dedicated Q1 2029 (finance ask). Due: 2028-11-09.
7) Evelyn Park — schedule a mid-week 30m "canary red-team" rehearsal (simulate rollback). Due: 2028-11-03.

Open questions / items to iterate on:
- Do we need a separate canary metric for token-level cost delta (per-request cost > baseline + 18%)? Action: Marcus to propose metric thresholds by 2028-11-04.
- Should we freeze non-critical infra merges during canary ramp window? Rina suggests targeted freeze for image changes and kernel-selection flags only. Team leaning toward targeted freeze.
- Long-term: evaluate automated rollback tiering that can scale partial capacity rollbacks (i.e., reduce to 30% of region) vs full rollback. Research owner: Marcus + Serving Runtime team.

Quick wins capture (to be executed this week):
- Increase image pull parallelism limit to reduce cold start impact (Rina)
- Add a short retention filter on noisy alert channel to reduce duplicate alert storms (Omar)
- Add conversational prompt family tag to canary evaluation harness (Sofia)

Follow-ups / next meeting:
- Quick readout on reproducer progress (Rina/Omar) — 2028-11-09 weekly leads meeting.
- Canary rehearsal outcomes (Evelyn) — 2028-11-03 midday checkpoint.
- Compliance checklist status (Priya) — 2028-11-06.

Appendix (raw notes / scratch):
- Slack thread with customer repro snippets: slack:#eng-leads ts:1720233300.000200 — contains prompt samples for fallback regression.
- Test harness link (internal): /ci/harnesses/cache-invalidation (see Confluence-1423 for pointer).
- Incident references: JIRA-SRE-8120 (alert storm on 2028-10-29), JIRA-ENG-7891 (kv cache repro).
